title: Conduction in metals, mobility, microscopic Ohm's law

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
In the gas (Drude) model, the free electrons in a metal zip around randomly at high thermal speed, bouncing off vibrating atoms and defects. With no field the random velocities average to zero, so there is no net current.

Apply a field \(E\) and each electron accelerates between collisions, but every collision scrambles its velocity again. On average the electrons pick up a small, constant **drift velocity** proportional to the field. The proportionality constant is the **mobility** \(\mu\), which is large when collisions are rare (long mean free time \(\tau_c\)) and the carrier is light. Current density is just charge density times drift velocity, and that gives Ohm's law in microscopic form: \(J = \sigma E\).

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ \bar u = -\mu E \ \text{(electrons)}, \qquad \mu = \frac{q\,\tau_c}{m^*} \]
\[ J = -q\,n\,\bar u = q\,n\,\mu\,E = \sigma E \]
\[ \sigma = q\,n\,\mu, \qquad \rho = \frac{1}{\sigma}, \qquad R = \rho\,\frac{L}{A} \]
Units used in this course: \(\mu\) in \(\mathrm{cm^2/(V\,s)}\), \(n\) in \(\mathrm{cm^{-3}}\), \(\rho\) in \(\Omega\,\mathrm{cm}\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
A conductor has \(n = 5\times10^{21}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}\) and \(\mu = 40\ \mathrm{cm^2/(V\,s)}\).
\[ \sigma = (1.602\times10^{-19})(5\times10^{21})(40) \approx 3.2\times10^{4}\ \mathrm{S/cm} \]
\[ \rho \approx 3.1\times10^{-5}\ \Omega\,\mathrm{cm} \]
In a field of 1 V/cm the drift speed is only \(40\ \mathrm{cm/s}\), tiny compared with thermal speeds near \(10^7\ \mathrm{cm/s}\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Thinking electrons accelerate forever in a steady field. Collisions cap the average speed.
- Mixing cm and m: \(1\ \mathrm{cm^2/(V\,s)} = 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2/(V\,s)}\).
- Forgetting the sign: electrons drift against \(E\), yet their current flows along \(E\).
- Confusing thermal (random) speed with drift speed.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Mobility and microscopic Ohm's law carry straight into semiconductors. Drift current, resistivity and the Einstein relation for diffusion all use the same \(\mu\), and the sawtooth picture of collisions explains why mobility falls when doping rises.
